episodes.172421: With an abundant amount of tropical moisture still in place over New Mexico, it was another very active day across New Mexico as scattered thunderstorms developed on September 13, 2022. Steering flow was a lot faster compared to recent previous days which limited the flash flooding threat. However, thunderstorm activity near Roswell produced a strong downburst which resulted in brief severe winds being measured at the airport in the city.
episodes.173129: A cold front moved through southern New England during the early evening triggering a few severe thunderstorms in northern Massachusetts.
episodes.173134: A warm front moved through southern New England during the morning bringing flooding to portions of Rhode Island.
episodes.173295: A stalled frontal boundary extended across NE FL, with heavy rainfall south of the front in convergent bands that moved onshore and extended inland from roughly St. Augustine southward toward Gainesville.
episodes.173695: An active pattern in mid-September resulted in several reports of flash flooding in southern Utah, in addition to some isolated thunderstorm related wind gusts in northern Utah.
episodes.173972: Isolated strong thunderstorms with concentrated heavy precipitation cores that initiated along the eastern Sierra caused periods of flash flooding and debris flows in and around the Holbrook Junction area that also closed  Nevada SR167 (Highland Way) to the Cal-Neva state line as well.
episodes.174044: Thunderstorms continued to develop along the eastern periphery of the mid-level circulation associated with the remnants of Hurricane Kay. The mid-level feature allowed thunderstorm development from early morning through the day.
episodes.174045: A trough just to the west of Arizona and southerly flow aloft helped produce scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. Some storms produced large hail, funnel clouds, and small tornadoes.
episodes.174067: A couple rounds of showers and thunderstorms resulted in heavy rain and flooding as well as some damaging wind reports (downed trees and powerlines) across eastern New York on September 13, 2022. Generally, one to three inches of rain fell across eastern New York with the heaviest amounts located over portions of Albany, Columbia, Rensselaer, Saratoga, Schoharie and Washington counties.
episodes.174068: Tropical Cyclone Kay formed on September 4th, 2022 and made its closest approach to Southern California on the 9th and 10th, with the center of Kay coming within 120 miles of San Diego. Tropical moisture associated with Kay managed to produce heavy rainfall leading to flooding across mountainous terrain in Southern California on September 9th and 10th. This led to a number of wind damage and flooding events in the mountains and desert foothill locations in Southern California. Kay transitioned to a Post-Tropical Cyclone that weekend, but left enough lingering moisture to support additional rounds of heavy thunderstorms through the 11th and 12th of September. These later rounds of heavy rain would lead to multiple significant debris flow events in the San Bernardino County Mountains, namely in and around the Apple and El Dorado burn scars.
episodes.174095: A cold front associated with a deep upper level low moved eastward into southwest Virginia during the afternoon, and into the Virginia Piedmont by late evening on September 12, 2022. Marginal instability increased with daytime heating, and when combined with plenty of deep layer moisture present in the atmosphere, resulted in scattered showers and a few thunderstorms. A couple of these storms produced damaging winds in Buckingham county.
episodes.174141: An occluded surface low drifted east-northeastward from northwestern OH to central Lake Erie during the early morning through early afternoon of the 13th. Isolated rain showers developed along a low-level convergence zone associated with the cyclonic circulation of the surface low. The ambient environment exhibited rich and deep low-level moisture, and lake-induced instability (e.g. lake surface to 850 mb temperature differences near 16C). The updraft of one of these lake-enhanced rain showers generated a non-mesocyclonic waterspout offshore metro Cleveland.
episodes.174285: A moist east to southeast wind flow led to the development of a few showers and thunderstorms over the Atlantic waters of SE Florida.
episodes.174344: Scattered thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Maryland Coastal Waters.
episodes.174346: Isolated severe thunderstorm in advance of a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.174369: A batch of moderate rainfall with embedded heavy thunderstorms moved through the area on September 13th bringing flash flooding to the New York City metro area. These thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front with a low pressure developing overhead in an extremely moisture environment that had precipitable water values of 1.8-2. These thunderstorms dropped between 1 and 3 inches of rainfall in a several hour period resulting in flash flooding.
episodes.174370: A batch of moderate rainfall with embedded heavy thunderstorms moved through the area on September 13th bringing flash flooding to the New York City metro area. These thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front with a low pressure developing overhead in an extremely moisture environment that had precipitable water values of 1.8-2. These thunderstorms dropped between 1 and 3 inches of rainfall in a several hour period resulting in flash flooding.
episodes.174381: A strong cold front moved through the area, with showers and thunderstorms develop out ahead of the front. A few of those thunderstorms were severe.
episodes.174570: A line of convection developed from central to southern New Hampshire ahead of an approaching cold front on the evening of September 13th.  The line became severe across southern New Hampshire and began to bow out bringing damaging wind gusts to Hillsbourgh County.
episodes.174607: The remnant circulation of former Pacific Hurricane Kay brought thunderstorms and flash flooding to the Mojave Desert.

Moderate to heavy rain fell across Zion National Park and surrounding areas, with 3-hour Multi-Radar/Multi-Sensor rainfall estimates of around 0.50 inches. As a result, the North Fork Virgin at Springdale river gauge recorded a rapid rise in stage from around 50 CFS to over 1200 CFS in under 2 hours. Additionally, park rangers at Zion National Park reported flooding in many slot canyons in the park, as well as several observed waterfalls.
